newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Tung heads for parley with Beijing.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Tung heads for parley with Beijing.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa will fly to Beijing on Wednesday for talks on the territory's July 1 takeover by China, a Tung aide said.
Tung would meet Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, the architect of Beijing's present policies on Hong Kong, and other senior Chinese officials.

Britain is handing Hong Kong back to China at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of colonial rule. It will become a quasi-autonomous capitalist region of communist-ruled China, and a Beijing-backed committee picked Tung as the first post-colonial leader.

There was speculation in the Hong Kong media that Tung would discuss the contentious issue of plans to curb civil liberties, the subject of a public pulse-taking exercise in the territory over the past month.
Hong Kong is deeply split over Tung's plan to curb the right to protest and to ban foreign funding of local political groups.
"We don't know his exact agenda in Beijing," the Tung aide said. "He is going to cover transition matters involving China, Hong Kong and Britain, and it could cover anything."
Tung will leave for Beijing early on Wednesday and return by late evening.
